cases.spec_ref: The data→AGS4 door (`build_ags4`) across all four surfaces. Each has its OWN input idiom — a polars frame (python), row-objects (node `buildAgs4`), a JSON string (wasm `build_ags4`), a `GroupInput` (rust-leaf) — but all route through the ONE shared emit orchestrator, so the built bytes (with the dictionary-filled UNIT/TYPE and the AutoFix-added TRAN/UNIT/TYPE groups) must be byte-identical. A surface re-implementing build would diverge from the leaf.

AGS4 numeric rendering is the ENGINE's job, from the declared TYPE: `laterite-types::ags4_str` formats a JSON number per its type (2DP `LOCA_NATE`: 12.3 -> `12.30`, 100.456 -> `100.46`), and every surface routes through it. A surface that stringified numbers itself — the obvious thing for a host binding to do — would emit `12.3` here and split from the leaf. NOTE: this case deliberately carries no INTEGER-valued cell. Adding one splits the node leg, which renders a whole JS number as `5.0` where rust/python/wasm render `5` (every JS number is an f64); that divergence is real and unresolved, so pin it in its own case once ruled on rather than smuggling it in here.

AGS4 Rule-1 field escaping (a literal `"` doubled to `""`, a comma kept inside the quoted field) has ONE authority — `laterite-types::write_quoted_field` — which the byte writer streams through and the browser tokenizer reuses. A surface re-implementing quoting would corrupt exactly this value.

A null cell is an EMPTY AGS4 field, not the string `null`/`None`/`NaN`. Each surface carries its own null idiom (polars null, JS null, JSON null, serde `Value::Null`) and they must all land on `""` via `ags4_str`'s null branch — the classic place a host binding leaks its own representation into the bytes.

A three-group build with a parent/child chain (PROJ -> LOCA -> SAMP): group ORDER is preserved as given, each group's UNIT/TYPE rows are filled from the dictionary, and the shared KEY heading `LOCA_ID` appears in both parent and child. Pins that no surface reorders groups or fills metadata differently.
